A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the C3/C3R research program and the same benchmark suite, and their supplied pages are readable. However, v2 includes Appendices A–F and a checklist, while the 11-page v3 ends with references despite citing appendices containing proofs, implementation details, and supplementary experiments. Those unavailable materials limit comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original C3R benchmark results, synthetic-data experiments, ablations, and sensitivity and efficiency analyses in Section 6 and Appendix F.

after.justification: v3 reports original results for its revised C3R method in Tables 1–2, synthetic-representation evaluation in Figure 3, and ablations in Figure 4.

M1.justification: v2 optimizes a minimax objective combining sufficiency, monotonicity, prior-KL, and independence constraints (Equation 14). v3 replaces this with an attention-derived instrumental variable, shared-parameter factual/counterfactual twin branches, gradient-based counterfactual construction, and C3 risk plus calibration and feasibility losses (Equations 6–10). This substantially changes both representation construction and optimization.

E1.justification: Both versions explicitly list the same six datasets: NYU Depth V2, SUN RGB-D, FOOD101, MVSA, BraTS, and MMLSynData. The documented coverage retains scene recognition, image-text classification, missing-modality segmentation, and synthetic SNC/SC/NC/SP evaluation, including noisy-input testing.

E2.justification: The comparator sets in Tables 1–2 and the synthetic boxplots are retained. v3 Figure 4 introduces an explicit original-MML-loss-only ablation control. However, v2 Tables 4–5 additionally evaluate unimodal comparators and more C3R combinations; v3's referenced supplementary comparisons are unavailable, preventing a reliable assessment of the full comparator-set change.

E3.justification: Table 1 changes the stated corruption unit from 50% of modalities in v2 to 50% of samples in v3. The ablation design also changes from six configurations of the old objective to four nested objectives, including the original MML loss alone. Dataset and metric coverage remain stable. These are reported protocol changes; the PDFs do not establish whether the corruption experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The central component ablation is redesigned: v2 Figure 3 examines sufficiency, monotonicity, and exogeneity penalties, whereas v3 Figure 4 evaluates the new C3 risk, instrumental-variable calibration, and feasibility penalty through nested objectives on FOOD101 and BraTS. The synthetic-correlation diagnostic remains. v2's additional spurious-correlation, efficiency, and sensitivity analyses cannot be fully matched because v3 Appendix H is unavailable.

E5.justification: Five runs are stated in v3 Section 6.1 but were already reported in v2 Table 3 and Appendices E–F. v2 Tables 4–5 also report numerical uncertainties, with captions describing three runs over 40 hyperparameter settings. Without v3's supplementary results, it is unclear whether those uncertainties and estimation procedures are retained or whether the inconsistent run descriptions were resolved.

E6.justification: C3R results are replaced throughout both main tables, and the redesigned ablation reports different outcomes. For example, QMF+C3R's clean NYU average changes from 76.56 to 77.58, and all-modality BraTS enhancing-tumour performance for LCKD+C3R changes from 85.45 to 86.36. Baseline table values remain unchanged. These are revised-method results with incompletely matched protocols, rather than established same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: v2's identification result requires exogeneity and monotonicity. v3 introduces non-exogeneity and instrumental-variable identification theorems, formal claims about attention-based instrument validity and twin-network estimation, and a Rademacher-complexity performance bound replacing the earlier distribution-shift and KL-based bounds. The mathematical framework changes substantially, although v3's cited proofs are unavailable.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion now claim causal identification and completeness without exogeneity and monotonicity, whereas v2 explicitly conditions its contribution on both assumptions. Instrumental-variable identification and reliable twin-network estimation become central contributions. The broader objective of plug-and-play causal-completeness regularization remains.

C2.justification: v2 Appendix B treats confounding-related corner cases as outside the principal analysis. v3 Sections 2–3 make coupled causal/non-causal factors and modality conflicts central applicability problems, explaining how the instrument and twin network are intended to address them. The causal-factor interpretation also shifts beyond modality-shared semantics. v2's explicit unsupervised-learning limitation is not repeated in the supplied v3 text.

D1.justification: v3 retains the reported MLP dimensions, optimizer, learning rate, and GPU, while documenting new loss weights of lambda_v = 0.75 and lambda_fe = 0.4. However, v2's appendices supply synthetic-data recipes, validation procedures, backbone details, and hyperparameter-search instructions whose v3 counterparts are unavailable. The overall extent of reproducibility-information changes therefore cannot be established.

R1.justification: v3 explicitly positions its contribution against Pearl's and Yang et al.'s assumption-dependent causal-sufficiency/necessity frameworks, emphasizing differences in identification, implementation, and objectives. v2 principally acknowledges inspiration while retaining those assumptions. New references such as Caner and Hansen on instrumental variables and Galles and Pearl on counterfactuals support this substantive repositioning.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, causal-development narrative, and related-work discussion are extensively rewritten. Section 2 becomes a fuller problem analysis, and Sections 3–5 are reorganized around identification, instrument construction, twin-network measurement, and the revised guarantee. The title and author list also change.

P2.justification: v3 reformats the paper from one column to two columns, relocates the duck example to the first page, adds the structural causal diagrams in Figure 2, and places both main tables together. The ablation figure is redrawn with different configurations, legends, and axes. These are substantial visual and layout changes beyond renumbering.

improvement.justification: v3 provides a more explicit causal-model explanation and a substantial redesign aimed at overcoming v2's restrictive assumptions. However, the proofs and supplementary validation needed to assess that advance are referenced but absent from the supplied PDF. Updated scores accompany method and protocol changes and do not independently establish better paper quality. The available evidence does not support a reliable net improvement or deterioration judgment.
